    All the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing. Our daily newsletter is a must-read from newsrooms to executive suites.

    Recent findings suggest that we will never sell your address. Prefer a weekly email?

    Nearly there — check your email.

    We have sent a confirmation link to . Click it and you are on the list. If it has not turned up in a minute or two, it may be in your spam folder.

    Meta will complete “a full consultation” with news industry leaders before implementing its controversial new terms — even if it means another delay, an executive for the social media company announced today.

    Industry observers note that “We’ve heard publishers’ feedback on our proposed ads and business terms patch. We care deeply about our partners and do not plan to make policy changes without a full consultation with industry groups and leaders,” vice president of communications Andy Stone tweeted. “We’re committed to getting this right, and as we expect this consultation could extend beyond November 20, in which case we’d delay implementation of the updated terms. Until then our existing terms remain in place.”.

    Meta did not answer Nieman Lab’s questions about which news industry groups and leaders Meta aims to consult.

    In a recent development, the proposed terms have drawn criticism because they would permit broad scraping of websites “associated with” business accounts, and potentially allow Meta to use that scraped content to train its AI models, with no option to opt out. Last week, Meta unveiled it would push back implementation of its new terms to November 20 in order to “explain to our partners and stakeholders what’s changing and what’s not — including how Meta uses web crawlers and the fact that content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal preferences,” a Meta spokesperson told Nieman Lab. Meta had previously revised its new terms to remove the word “train.” No version of the terms has included language about respecting robots.txt preferences.

    Shortly after Stone’s announcement, a Norwegian court blocked Meta’s terms from taking effect on November 20 until the court had assessed their legality, the country’s public broadcaster NRK reported.

    “We are satisfied that the court has agreed with us that Meta holds a dominant position in the relevant market and that the fresh terms are unreasonable,” mentioned Lene Eltvik Vindfeld, MBL’s board chair, in a news release. “We are also pleased that the court recognizes that the alternative is that media companies risk losing control over editorial content built up over many years.”.

    Since Nieman Lab first reported on the terms on October 15, publishers and politicians around the world have pushed back, filing complaints with national competition authorities, calling on the European Commission to investigate, and writing letters to Meta’s CEO Mark Zuckerberg. Two United States senators — California Democrat Adam Schiff and Tennessee Republican Marsha Blackburn — each separately wrote to Zuckerberg, insisting that the company withdraw the terms as they’re right now written.

    “After I raised serious concerns about Meta’s looks to scrape and abuse creators’ content, I am pleased the organization is finally acknowledging the concerns of publishers and content creators,” Blackburn remarked in a statement to Nieman Lab on Wednesday. “While this is a step in the right direction, a vague promise to consult with industry stakeholders and potentially delay implementation is not nearly enough. Meta must commit to meaningful changes that protect the intellectual property rights of American creators, and I will continue holding the company accountable until it does.”.

    Recent findings suggest that on October 21, the European Publishers Council signed onto a joint letter to the European Commission, asking the Commission to block the terms from taking effect. The letter claims that Meta’s terms violate the Digital Markets Act, a law passed in 2020 to curb the dominance of big tech companies and create fairer competition across the region.

    EPC executive director Angela Mills Wade stated on Wednesday that the organization has not heard from Meta about its letter or its concerns.

    Industry observers note that “We welcome Meta’s offer to consult publishers fully, and to delay implementation if necessary,” Mills Wade remarked in an email to Nieman Lab. “However, that consultation must lead to binding contractual safeguards…Using Meta’s services to reach audiences or advertise should not mean granting wider rights to exploit publishers’ journalism, whether collected from websites or uploaded to its platforms. Publishers must retain control over additional uses of their content, including for AI, and the ability to negotiate licenses and payment.”.

    This story has been updated to include a statement from Marsha Blackburn.

    Latest Update: Head of Ecosystem at Supabase

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers.
    • We're looking for a Head of Ecosystem to lead the teams that make Supabase the backend for the platforms and tools developers already use.
    • You'll also drive hiring, onboarding, and career development while maintaining high engineering standards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We aim to empower developers by providing a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    We're looking for a Head of Ecosystem to lead the teams that make Supabase the backend for the platforms and tools developers already use. That covers AI app builders and coding agents, integrations with the developer tools teams rely on, and the Supabase Marketplace. You'll build this org from the ground up and shape how Supabase extends beyond its own platform.

    You'll also drive hiring, onboarding, and career development while maintaining high engineering standards.

    Build and lead a newly introduced engineering org across platform partners, integrations, and Marketplace, hiring EMs and engineers as it grows.

    Own the technical relationship with the platforms building on Supabase, from integration health to escalations.

    Set and maintain clear roadmaps that balance partner needs with platform priorities.

    Partner with Product, Partnerships, and Sales to define and execute our ecosystem strategy.

    Ship a unified, self-serve surface for integrations and Marketplace.

    Maintain high engineering standards: roadmap hygiene, concern tracking, on-call, incident response, and responsiveness to partners.

    Proven experience leading multiple engineering teams, including managing other managers.

    Experience building and running platform, API, or integration surfaces that third parties depend on in production.

    Technical credibility with partner engineering teams, and the judgment to say no.

    Experience building teams or an org from a small base, including hiring and developing engineering managers.

    Strong organizational and execution skills: setting roadmaps, driving accountability, and keeping teams moving under uncertainty.

    Experience managing remote, globally distributed teams.

    Excellent cross-functional communication skills, especially with Product and commercial teams.

    Collaborative, low-ego, and adaptable.

    Have experience with OAuth, platform APIs, or app marketplaces.

    Have worked on a developer platform's partner or app ecosystem.

    Have worked with AI app builders or coding agents.

    Industry observers note that we hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the manufacturer. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Industry observers note that supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

    In a recent development, once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    Recent findings suggest that supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.
